correctness.rationale: For U in (0,1)^2 and radius R<1, all integer sites inside the disk belong to the four enclosing square vertices. The squared-distance parallelogram identity rules out an included diagonal pair without any point of the other diagonal; consequently the area is (I_diagonal1+I_diagonal2)/2. A diagonal event has ordinary equal-circle lens area L_R and the four-corner event has exact intersection area Q_R obtained by integrating the largest-corner-distance inequality x²+y²+|x|+|y|<=R²-1/2. Inclusion-exclusion yields exactly masses (1-2L+Q,2(L-Q),Q) on (0,1/2,1). Independent numerical slicing agreed with closed L,Q at R=.75,.82,.99 to <5e-7. Near onset δ=R²-1/2, lens geometry gives L~4sqrt(2)/3 δ^(3/2), fourfold diamond gives Q~2δ². The R=1/sqrt(2) measure-zero boundary is treated, and R>=1 is excluded. Monte Carlo/grids corroborate, not prove, continuous formula.
residual_risks: The word boundary length is defined only for two-dimensional hulls, with zero by convention for degenerate hulls.
The formula does not extend at R>=1, where additional lattice points have positive chance to enter.

value.rationale: Radius 1/sqrt2 is the exact first radius for a two-dimensional random lattice hull and R<1 the canonical four-corner chamber. Complete three-atom area and boundary-length laws and distinct triangular/square onset exponents quantify the birth of nondegenerate digital convex hulls, not an arbitrary one-off numeric integral.
residual_risks: Restricted to square lattice, disk, uniform shift and first small-radius chamber.
